display_name: Catena Zapata High Mountain Vines Malbec, Mendoza
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Lunlunta's gravelly alluvial soils stress Malbec vines at nearly 1,000 meters, yielding small berries packed with black fruit concentration. Catena Zapata blends Cot (Malbec), Cabernet Sauvignon, and Chardonnay here to layer density with citrus-driven lift. Diurnal swings of 15-20°C lock in acidity amid ripe plum flavors.",
  "wine_summary": "Catena Zapata mapped Mendoza's altitude bands in the 1990s, proving high sites beat lowland heat for balanced Malbec. This High Mountain Vines edition pulls from Lunlunta parcels, blending Cot-dominant fruit with Cabernet structure and Chardonnay snap for a red that defies simple varietal boxes. The result channels Andean purity: intense color from thin-skinned grapes, floral lift from cool exposure.",
  "terroir_expression": "Lunlunta's alluvial gravels, deposited by Mendoza River floods, drain fast and warm roots by day, concentrating blackberry and cassis while gravel minerality threads the finish. Semi-arid continental climate delivers 250mm annual rain, forcing drip irrigation from Andean snowmelt; nights drop to 10°C, preserving malic acidity for plum skin tension over soft earth notes.",
  "vinification_summary": "Hand-harvested clusters ferment in concrete tanks with pied-de-cuve native yeasts—a vineyard-specific starter culture that amplifies site differences without commercial strains. Cabernet lots gain oak barrel structure, Chardonnay co-ferments briefly for texture, then the blend rests 12 months in French oak to integrate tannins. Choices prioritize parcel transparency over heavy extraction.",
  "food_pairing": "Grilled Argentine asado ribs with chimichurri: tannins grip fatty beef while acidity slices herbs. Nashville hot chicken tenders: citrus lift from Chardonnay tempers cayenne burn, fruit matches fried crust. Osso buco Milanese with gremolata: earth tannins echo braised marrow, high-altitude acid refreshes saffron rice. Wood-fired pepperoni pizza: gravelly cut-through powers cheese grease. Gorgonzola-stuffed burger: Cabernet depth binds blue funk, Malbec fruit bridges beef char.",
  "comparable_wines": "Altos las Hormigas Appellation Gualtallary Malbec — matches high-altitude gravel focus and diurnal freshness. Zuccardi Valle de Uco Malbec — similar Andean alluvial drive with blended structure. Bodega Colome Malbec — altitude purity echoes in black fruit and mineral spine.",
  "style_profile": "Full-bodied dry red with firm tannins and floral-mineral lift",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Open 2025-2033 as tannins soften into silk. Keep bottles horizontal at 55°F, 70% humidity in darkness.",
  "value_assessment": "$20-25 at Spec's undercuts Catena's single-vineyard Adrianna Malbecs ($50+). Outpaces Alamos Malbec ($15, flatter fruit) in depth from old vines. Stock up—altitude quality punches above budget weight.",
  "market_position": "Retail racks position it for Malbec explorers stepping past $10 bottles. Neighborhood steakhouses pour it with dry-aged ribeyes. Home cooks grab for weekend grills, not auction hype.",
  "insider_take": "Chardonnay inclusion trades Malbec purity for brighter midpalate snap that casual drinkers crave. Most fixate on oak but miss how gravels anchor the core. Buy for versatile power; skip if seeking 100% Cot focus.",
  "aging_potential_years": 8,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 1,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 10,
